{{Short description|Soviet and American mathematician (born 1934)}}
{{family name hatnote|Solomonovich|Schwarz|lang=Eastern Slavic}}
'''Albert Solomonovich Schwarz'''<ref>Credited as ''Schwartz'' in A. A. Belavin ''et al'' (1975).</ref> ({{IPAc-en|ʃ|w|ɔr|t|s}} {{respell|SHWORTS}}; {{langx|ru|Альберт Соломонович Шварц}}; born June 24, 1934) is a Soviet-American mathematician and a theoretical physicist educated in the Soviet Union and now a professor at the [[University of California, Davis]].

==Early life and education==
Schwarz was born in [[Kazan]] to [[Ashkenazi Jewish]] parents, [[Soviet Union]]. His parents were arrested in the [[Stalinist purges]] in 1937.<ref>{{cite web |title=My life in science |url=https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~schwarz/bion.pdf |website=ucdavis.edu |access-date=18 May 2023}}</ref>

Schwarz studied under [[Vadim Yefremovich]] at Ivanovo Pedagogical Institute, having been denied admittance to [[Moscow State University]] on the grounds that he was the son of "[[enemies of the people]]."<ref>{{cite web | title=Albert Schwarz | website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project | url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=12690 | access-date=18 May 2023}}</ref>

==Career and later life==
After defending his dissertation in 1958, he took a job at Voronezh University. In 1964 he was offered a job at [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/ideas/2011/witten-knots-quantum-theory|title = Knots and Quantum Theory - Ideas &#124; Institute for Advanced Study|date = 5 August 2011}}</ref> He immigrated to the United States in 1989.<ref>{{Cite book|isbn = 978-9813278639|title = Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Field Theory|last1 = Schwarz|first1 = Albert|year = 2020}}</ref>

==Contributions==
Schwarz is one of the pioneers of [[Morse theory]] and brought up the first example of a [[topological quantum field theory]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Albert+Schwarz|title = Albert Schwarz in nLab}}</ref> The Schwarz genus, one of the fundamental notions of [[topological complexity]], is named after him.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Vassiliev | first = V. A.
 | issue = 3
 | journal = Moscow Mathematical Journal
 | mr = 2894434
 | pages = 617–625, 632
 | title = Topological complexity and Schwarz genus of general real polynomial equation
 | volume = 11
 | year = 2011}}</ref> Schwarz worked on some examples in [[noncommutative geometry]]. He is the "S" in the [[AKSZ theory|AKSZ model]] (named after Mikhail Alexandrov, [[Maxim Kontsevich]], Schwarz, and Oleg Zaboronski).<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Cattaneo | first1 = Alberto S.
 | last2 = Felder | first2 = Giovanni
 | doi = 10.1023/A:1010963926853
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Letters in Mathematical Physics
 | mr = 1854134
 | pages = 163–179
 | title = On the AKSZ formulation of the Poisson sigma model
 | volume = 56
 | year = 2001}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1990, Schwarz was an invited speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Kyoto]]. He was elected to the 2018 class of [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2018 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2017-11-03}}</ref>

==Monographs==
* ''Topology for physicists'', Springer, 1996.
* ''Quantum field theory and topology'', Grundlehren der Math. Wissen. 307, Springer 1993 (translated from Russian original ''Kvantovaja teorija polja i topologija, Nauka'', Moscow, 1989).
* A. S. Švarc, ''Математические основы квантовой теории поля (Mathematical aspects of quantum field theory)'', Atomizdat, Moscow, 1975.
*''Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Field Theory'', 2020.

==Papers (selection)==

* A. S. Švarc, Род расслоенного пространства, ''Докл''. ''АН СССР'' (The genus of a fiber space (Russian), [[Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR]] '''119''' (1958), no. 2,  219–222.
* A. Schwarz, O. Zaboronsky, Supersymmetry and localization, ''Comm. Math. Phys.'' '''183'''(2) (1997), 463–476.
* M. Alexandrov, M. Kontsevich, A. Schwarz, O. Zaboronsky, The geometry of the master equation and topological quantum field theory, ''Int. J. Modern Phys''. '''A12'''(7):1405–1429, 1997.
* V. Kac, A. Schwarz, Geometric interpretation of the partition function of 2D gravity, ''Phys. Lett.'' '''B257''' (1991), nos. 3–4, 329–334.
* A. A. Belavin, A. M. Polyakov, A. S. Schwartz, Yu. S. Tyupkin, Pseudoparticle solutions of the Yang-Mills equations, ''Phys. Lett.'' '''B59''' (1975), no. 1, 85–87.
* V. N. Romanov, A. S. Švarc, Anomalies and elliptic operators (Russian), ''Teoret. Mat. Fiz.'' '''41''' (1979), no. 2, 190–204.
* S. N. Dolgikh, A. A. Rosly, A. S. Schwarz, Supermoduli spaces, ''Comm. Math. Phys.'' '''135''' (1990), no. 1, 91–100.
